newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hermes sees rise in 1997 profits.
newsitem.headline: Hermes sees rise in 1997 profits.

text.p: French luxury goods firm Hermes expects to report a growth in profits for the current financial year, financial director Mireille Maury said in an interview.
"There will be an increase in profits in 1997 but we are not saying more for the moment," she told Reuters.
The company reported 1996 net attributable profit of 457.0 million francs, up 13.1 percent from the previous year.
Maury also said the group expects to boost investments this year.
"We have a total investment budget for 1997 of about 400 million francs as well as an exceptional investment of 450 million planned for Japan between 1997 and 1999," she said.
The Japanese exceptional investment will be used to set up a boutique in Tokyo. The opening is set for end 1999.
In 1996, the group's investments totalled 557 million francs but that included 250 million francs in exceptional investments.
For 1997, Hermes is covered by an option on the dollar at a minimum rate of 5.40 francs and at 5.35 francs on the yen, Maury said.
Sales in silk should be stable in 1997 but grow significantly in leather and ready-to-wear, she said.
For the first quarter of 1997, sales rose 14.4 percent to 1.08 billion francs.
The company said it has no plans for any acquisitions.
Hermes' capital is 80 percent controlled by family interests. It employs 4,000 people around the world.
